hero.title: A Mechanism-First Method, With the Limits Stated Plainly.
hero.lead: Most dream interpretation has a methodology problem. The method is: look up the symbol, return the meaning. Fast, scalable, and completely indifferent to the person who had the dream.
hero.lead_strong: The person who had the dream matters. The science also has limits. Oneirox separates established sleep physiology, supported associations, and interpretation instead of pretending one dream can be decoded like a lab result.

origin.title: The Gap Between What People Say and What the Body Registers
origin.quote: The image is never the point. The feeling that generated the image is the point. I start there.
origin.disclaimer: I am not a clinician. I am not a therapist. I'm a researcher with an obsession and a methodology. This is not a medical resource.

principles.title: The Emotional Signature Comes Before the Symbol Table.
principles.body: Dream research does not show that a dream image has a fixed biological meaning. Oneirox starts with felt quality and waking context because emotion and salience are measurable parts of sleep mentation while symbolic decoding remains interpretive.

principles.title: Waking Body Signals Are Context, Not Proof.
principles.body: Chest pressure, jaw tension, temperature, immobility, or a jolt can be useful observations because sleep physiology can cross the wake boundary. They can constrain an interpretation, but they do not prove what a dream meant.
principles.citation: REM physiology + interoceptive context; dream-specific inference remains a hypothesis

principles.title: Mechanism and Life Context Must Stay Separate.
principles.body: Sleep stage, arousal, memory reactivation, and autonomic state can shape dream experience. Waking concerns can also be incorporated into dreams. Oneirox uses both layers without claiming that a specific image uniquely identifies a specific neural mechanism.
principles.citation: Siclari et al. 2017 · Salvesen et al. 2024

principles.title: Timing Can Be Informative, Not Diagnostic.
principles.body: Dreams often incorporate recent or salient waking experience, but there is no validated rule that a dream appearing before a life event diagnoses that event. Timing is context that may raise or lower a hypothesis.
principles.citation: Dream-incorporation literature; effect sizes and methods vary

principles.title: A Dream Is Not Prophecy — and It Is Not a Neural Readout.
principles.body: Current neuroscience does not support fixed dream dictionaries or a method that can infer one hidden message from one dream. Oneirox returns a working explanation: what is established, what is plausible, and what remains speculative.
principles.citation: Siclari et al. 2017 · Bloxham 2024 · Valli & Revonsuo 2009

reading_sequence.title: The Feeling
reading_sequence.text: What is the felt quality of the dream, and what did the body feel like on waking? Record these as observations, not as proof of meaning.

reading_sequence.title: The Timing
reading_sequence.text: What waking-life material was recent, salient, or emotionally loaded? Treat timing as context, not diagnosis.

reading_sequence.title: The Neuroscience
reading_sequence.text: Which sleep mechanisms could plausibly contribute — and which claims are established versus still hypothetical?

reading_sequence.title: The Specificity
reading_sequence.text: What distinguishes this version of the dream from other versions of the same image?

reading_sequence.title: The Working Interpretation
reading_sequence.text: State the narrowest explanation consistent with the evidence. Label what is established, supported, or speculative; do not pretend certainty.

timeline.title: Foundation — Walker, Cartwright, LeDoux
timeline.text: Dreaming is not random, but neither dream function nor dream meaning has one settled neural explanation. That uncertainty became part of the method.

timeline.title: The Body Layer — Damasio, Sapolsky, Porges
timeline.text: Body-state observations can add useful context, but they are not a decoder key. The method began separating physiology from interpretation.

timeline.title: The Depth Layer — Jung, van der Kolk, Levine
timeline.text: Recurring dreams, nightmares, and trauma-related sleep showed why clinical phenomena and symbolic interpretation must not be collapsed into one claim.

timeline.title: Building Oneirox
timeline.text: Cluster architecture connected related dream themes while keeping shared mechanisms separate from page-specific interpretation.

timeline.title: Tools. Instruments. The Lab.
timeline.text: Sensory Dream Mapper and Lab Search became tools for organizing observations and hypotheses — not instruments that diagnose a hidden message.

limitations.title: What This Methodology Cannot Do
limitations.closing: What it can do is organize the evidence, surface plausible mechanisms, and give you a disciplined question to test against your own experience. The final interpretation remains a hypothesis.

evidence_standard.established: Directly supported sleep physiology or replicated observational finding.
evidence_standard.supported_hypothesis: Plausible interpretation with empirical support but meaningful uncertainty.
evidence_standard.speculative: Oneirox interpretation or theory that must not be presented as a biological fact.
